items.description: A catalogue entry combining two distinct sources: (1) the Dictionary of Welsh Biography entry for Alfred Thomas, 1st Baron Pontypridd, which identifies him as Daniel Thomas's son and dates his death, unmarried, to 14 December 1927; and (2) a secondary online transcription of a newspaper report dated 27 December 1927, which describes an “unofficial report” that the bulk of his property was left to Cardiff Corporation and citizens. These sources have different verification status and must not be collapsed into one verified claim.
items.transcript: The Dictionary of Welsh Biography wording quoted in the catalogue is: “Born 16 September 1840, at Llwyn-y-grant, Pen-y-lan, Cardiff, son of Daniel Thomas, contractor … He died, unmarried, 14 December 1927.” The secondary transcription reports: “The unofficial report is that the bulk of his property, has been, left unconditionally to the corporation, and citizens” of Cardiff. The original newspaper and its full bibliographic identity have not been established from the transcription.
items.interpretation: The death date and father-son identification are supported by the Dictionary of Welsh Biography. This creates a real chronological discrepancy with Mary (Nancy) Williams's c.1974 statement that the last rent payment was made “to Alfred Thomas the son of Daniel Thomas” in 1928. The statement does not prove Alfred personally received money after his death; the estate, an executor or agent, a receipt continuing to use Alfred's name, or an error in the remembered date/payee remain possibilities. The Corporation bequest is a secondary report explicitly described as unofficial. “The bulk of his property” does not establish that Great House Farm, a freehold interest at Llandough, or any specific land parcel formed part of the estate. Nor does the absence of a located Llandough transfer prove that nothing passed to the Corporation. The will, grant, original newspaper, Thomas estate accounts, Cardiff Corporation deeds/property registers and relevant minutes must be checked before making a land-title inference.
items.interpretation_status: working interpretation; source distinction and limits stated
items.source_verification_status: Death and identity supported by Dictionary of Welsh Biography; secondary estate report unverified; will/grant and original newspaper not inspected
items.limitations: Do not state that the Corporation inherited Great House Farm or that it inherited nothing. The press transcription says “bulk of his property” and calls the report unofficial; it does not identify the assets. A research note cites a reported grant date of 8 March 1928 and London Gazette notice of 30 March 1928, p.2387, but the primary grant and will have not been inspected. The separate 23 February 1905 Bute-to-Cardiff Corporation conveyance is a competing title-chain lead and must not be conflated with Alfred's estate.

items.description: A pending evidence item for the receipt Mary (Nancy) Williams says she saw for the last rent payment, recalled as made by her father in 1928, of about £4 per annum, to “Alfred Thomas the son of Daniel Thomas”, when quarry machinery was removed. The receipt itself has not been located; the available source is Mary's later witness statement.
items.transcript: Mary (Nancy) Williams's c.1974 statement: “The quarry had practically ceased to operate when I was born but I remember that there was still machinery at the quarry until 1928 when the machinery was removed and the last payment of rent was made to Alfred Thomas the son of Daniel Thomas. I remember that this payment was made by my father and that the rent was then about £4 per annum. I saw the receipt for this last payment of rent. After this my father regarded the farm as his own …”
items.transcript_status: transcribed from the later witness statement; original 1928 receipt not held
items.interpretation: This is evidence of what Mary later recalled and of her statement that she had seen a receipt, not direct inspection of the receipt. Alfred Thomas's independently recorded death on 14 December 1927 means the remembered 1928 date and named recipient need reconciliation. The actual payee, payment date, collecting person, land description, whether the payment covered rent or quarry-related rights, and legal effect are unresolved. The 10 November 1925 sale catalogue for quarry plant and tramlines (Glamorgan Archives DSA/12/4888) is a separate lead; it does not prove the machinery was removed in 1925. The Court of Appeal's references to rent arrears and a 1953 payment must be mapped to the relevant tenancy and parcel before treating them as a contradiction.
items.source_verification_status: Mary's statement located/transcribed; receipt not located; payment details not independently verified
items.limitations: Do not describe the receipt as held, authenticated, or inspected. Preserve Mary's exact wording. The possibilities of payment to an estate/executor/agent, a receipt using Alfred's name, or a remembered date/payee error are alternatives only; none is established. The parcel extent and relationship to the 1877 instrument remain unverified.

items.description: Catalogue entry for a family-supplied photograph of an inscription reading “John Williams” with “1886” beneath, catalogued as a visual comparator for the tenant signature on the 1939 Western Ground Rents tenancy agreement (EV-0023). Only the comparator crop is included; the object identity and location are not disclosed.
items.transcript: The crop shows the words “John Williams” with “1886” beneath.
items.interpretation: Visible form only: the inscription has an ornate capital J, wide letter spacing and an extended stroke over the final letters; the 1939 signature on EV-0023 is more compact with tighter letter spacing. These are surface observations of a photograph, not an authentication: a visible difference between an inscription and a signature does not establish different writers, and the comparison cannot establish who signed the 1939 agreement. Authorship, date and object identity are unverified.
items.source_verification_status: photograph read; original object not inspected; authorship and date unverified
items.limitations: Family-stated provenance only. A photograph of an inscription is not a signature exemplar; no handwriting conclusion is drawn. The original photograph has not been independently inspected.

items.description: One-page HM Land Registry Wales Office letter dated 4 November 2026, HMLR reference Z084NQV, concerning title WA231076. The recipient-supplied PDF was visually inspected. The public evidence copy is a transcription; the recipient email address and one-time secure-document URL are omitted.
items.transcript:
HM LAND REGISTRY — WALES OFFICE
Letter dated 4 November 2026
HMLR reference: Z084NQV
Your reference: 260927-6756312
Title number: WA231076
Property: Land on the north side of Leckwith Road, Llandough
Proprietor/applicant: Persimmon Homes (Wales) Limited

PUBLIC TRANSCRIPTION
The recipient email address and the one-time secure-document URL are omitted from this public copy. The wording below follows the one-page PDF supplied by the recipient. The line “Regarding you letter” is retained as it appears in the source.

Dear Customer

Regarding you letter of 12 August 2026 and using the same numbering for ease of reference

1. We have provided you with a list of documents retained by HM Land Registry which are available for inspection.
2. The statement is contained in the application for first registration (1E)
3.-7. Please see reply to 1 above.

Regarding your further correspondence of 15 October 2026, we have already explained to you that no application for alteration or indemnity may be considered and our reasons for this; please see letters of 19 April and 25 May 2026. These letters together with the letter of 23 March 2026 set out relevant history of the title and first registration of the land. As per the above, we have provided a list of documents available for inspection relating to the Property. It is important to understand that the Registrar cannot provide an interpretation / explanation of the deeds or any legal advice. There is nothing further that we can usefully add to what has already been said. The appropriate forum for any further action is the Court and not HM Land Registry.

Yours faithfully,

Charlotte Takeuchi
Assistant Land Registrar

PROVENANCE AND LIMITS
One-page PDF received by the addressee through HM Land Registry’s electronic notification on 4 November 2026. This public text is a transcription, not a facsimile of the PDF. The individual secure document URL and recipient email address are not reproduced. The PDF itself is not embedded in this public transcription page.

It acknowledges the 15 October correspondence but does not identify a notice or disclose its date, addressee, address, dispatch method or proof of service for WA240304. The absence of those details in this letter does not establish that no notice was issued.
